title: Fractional per-terminal cap (0.2 pkts/tick) is unenforceable as a per-tick integer comparison — every residential spawn would be skipped
evidence: stories-v2.md:658: "- **When** a spec's volume would assign more spawns to one terminal than its cap this tick;" · spec-traffic-model.md:118: "  starting point: **~0.2 pkts/tick** for a residential ≈ 6 u/s demand vs the ~8–10 u/s access link" · spec-traffic-model.md:120: "- The cap is a **hard bound on the variance**, not the average: the director's weighted-random pick" · core/flow.odin:646: "for k in 0..<vol {"
detail: Spawns are integer per tick (flow.odin:646); a per-tick hard cap of 0.2 rejects every single spawn (1 > 0.2), so residential-sourced email (demand.json volume 4) never lands. No accumulator/token-bucket mechanism is specified anywhere; the (20 ÷ cap) formula only coheres with one.
recommended_fix: Specify the enforcement mechanism: a per-terminal spawn accumulator (state home + T1 hash noted) or integer form (e.g. 1 spawn per N ticks); state the determinism implications of the new run state.

title: Proposed group radius (~2–3 tiles) collides with GROWTH_MIN_SEP_TILES=3 — in-group candidates always fail E31 min-separation
evidence: spec-traffic-model.md:169: "Proposed starting shape: 3–8 terminals per group; group radius ~2–3 tiles (see the conflict" · core/growth.odin:76: "GROWTH_MIN_SEP_TILES :: i32(3)" · core/growth.odin:166: "		if i64(d[0])*i64(d[0]) + i64(d[1])*i64(d[1]) < sep2 {"
detail: growth_node_sep_ok rejects any candidate within 3 tiles of every live node, so a 2-tile-radius biased candidate is always E31-invalid — the group bias silently no-ops via rejection sampling; radius 3 sits exactly at the floor, and player-wired pipes add further 3-tile exclusion. The spec's 'conflict resolution' addresses only bias-vs-envelope ordering, not these constants.
recommended_fix: Set the group radius strictly above GROWTH_MIN_SEP_TILES (≥4 tiles, also clearing GROWTH_OUT_MIN_TILES and pipe segments), or document the min-sep interaction and its packing consequences in the conflict resolution.

title: Sink-side concentration is unbounded — dst picks can still self-congest a residential's own access pipe, falsifying the absolute 'endpoints never self-congest' invariant
evidence: gdd.md:306: "   fraction of its access capacity, so **endpoints never self-congest** — the invariant everything" · core/flow.odin:650: "				didx, okd := weighted_pick_excluding(&state.rng, sink_ids[:], sink_w[:], src)" · core/flow.odin:718: "			if bundle_lane_count(state, cat, b, lane, drops[:]) >= u32(cat.balance.lane_queue_packets) {" · data/demand.json:49: "\"sink_role\": \"residential\","
detail: Caps bind only source spawning; dst selection stays unbounded weighted-random. Under the surge (20/tick onto few residential sinks on a small map), inbound volume (≥30 u/pkt) exceeds the ~8–10 u/tick access drop and E9 sheds at the endpoint's own pipe — the exact noise M6 claims eliminated.
recommended_fix: Bound per-terminal dst picks per tick with the same cap machinery, or scope the M6 invariant explicitly to source-side self-congestion and name the sink-side path.

title: Thread 4's 'a data change, not a code change' is false — Terminal_Role is a closed enum and new roles fail catalog load
evidence:
gdd.md:319: "   catalog data (`node_types.json`) — a data change, not a code change; distinct shape/icon per type," · core/catalog.odin:22: "Terminal_Role :: enum u8 { None, Residential, Content_Host }" · core/catalog.odin:365-367: "			if nt.kind == .Terminal && nt.terminal_role == .None {
				return {"node_types.json", nt.id, "terminal without a role"}" · role_from_name (catalog.odin:1011-1016) returns .None for any name but "residential"/"content_host"
detail: Adding small_biz/campus entries with new terminal_role strings fails load until the enum + role_from_name + selector code is extended; the per-type cap/profile fields are also inert until loader code reads them (the loaded-not-consumed anti-pattern the spec itself flags for bandwidth_demand).
recommended_fix: Qualify the claim ('roster values are data; new roles + cap fields are code') and name the Terminal_Role enum, role_from_name, and loader extension in card 5.11.

title: Headroom derivation misattributes streaming volume to residential sources
evidence: spec-traffic-model.md:61: "residential emitting ~**0.2 pkts/tick** (its share of 6/tick across ~30 terminals) fits with" · data/demand.json:48: "\"source_role\": \"content_host\"," (streaming sources from content_host, not residential)
detail: Residential share of the 6/tick era-3 arrivals is only the email 4/tick (≈0.13 across 30 terminals); streaming is content_host-sourced. The cap number itself still bounds the share, but the stated derivation is wrong.
recommended_fix: Recompute the share as 4/tick residential-sourced email, or restate the cap as 'chosen above the expected per-terminal share'.

title: Access-tier headroom assumes exactly one access pipe — unlimited terminal ports and parallel-pipe bundling leave dual-homed/bundled access topology unaddressed
evidence: spec-traffic-model.md:74: "- **Given** a residential terminal connected by a single narrow pipe to its aggregation point;" · data/node_types.json:2: "port_capacity 0 = unlimited (terminals)" · gdd.md:153: "multiple pipes can connect the same node pair — and parallel pipes **bundle into one pooled-capacity link** whose capacity is the **sum** of the bundled pipes' capacities"
detail: A player can dual-home a residential or bundle two narrows; the spec never states whether the ≥1.3–1.5× headroom invariant is per-pipe or per-terminal-bundle, and the 'cost ladder is moot (a single path)' rationale fails for dual-homed terminals.
recommended_fix: State the invariant's unit (per access bundle, summed capacity) and note the dual-homed case where path alternatives make the cost ladder live at the terminal.
